# PragOptics

> PragOptics is the field-data, calibration, and visualization platform for industrial automation, and the maker of OmniBus, a universal, vendor-neutral handheld HART communicator, calibration recorder, and field node. PragOptics is a Fortiview Holdings brand.

## What OmniBus is

OmniBus works any HART instrument across manufacturers over USB HART, an on-board two-wire loop, HART-IP, and Wi-Fi. It measures true 4-20 mA loop current on board, turns every connection into a guided As-Found / As-Left calibration record with auto-generated certificates and an append-only audit trail, and reaches wireless gateways with multi-modal HART-IP that auto-detects a gateway host versus a single instrument.

## HART resources

- [What is HART?](https://pragoptics.com/hart/what-is-hart/): How HART communication works: the 4-20 mA loop, masters, device variables, commands, DD/DTM, HART-IP, and calibration.
- [HART communicator](https://pragoptics.com/hart/hart-communicator/): What a HART communicator is, the three form factors, primary vs secondary master, and how to choose one.
- [HART calibration](https://pragoptics.com/hart/hart-calibration/): As-Found / As-Left, trim types, tolerance and NE43, and a step-by-step calibration procedure.
- [HART-IP](https://pragoptics.com/hart/hart-ip/): HART over Ethernet, gateway hosts versus direct instruments, and wireless mesh.
- [HART vs 4-20 mA](https://pragoptics.com/hart/hart-vs-4-20ma/): Why HART rides on top of the analog loop instead of replacing it.
- [WirelessHART](https://pragoptics.com/hart/wirelesshart/): The IEC 62591 mesh, gateways, adapters, and how it relates to wired HART and HART-IP.
- [HART commands](https://pragoptics.com/hart/hart-commands/): Universal, common-practice, and device-specific commands, and why they enable universal tools.
- [HART glossary](https://pragoptics.com/hart/glossary/): Key HART terms defined, from Bell 202 FSK and PV/SV/TV/QV to As-Found / As-Left.
- [HART FAQ](https://pragoptics.com/hart/faq/): Straight, answer-first responses to the HART questions technicians actually ask.
